audit_findings.title: Completed ElevATE acquisition makes the pre-close bridge perimeter-incoherent
audit_findings.magnitude: $250.0 million base consideration, subject to adjustments, plus up to $50.0 million earnout; $250.0 million equals 17.4% of base equity value or $5.28 per diluted share; final effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes cash, debt, assumed liabilities, interest expense, owner earnings, and the operating perimeter after the June 30 balance-sheet date.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary sources of liquidity are cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, funds from operations, and, if necessary, borrowings under our credit facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated dating and perimeter error: ElevATE closed August 27, 2026, before the September 6 valuation, while the valuation retains June 30 cash and debt and excludes ElevATE's operations. The stale cash addition could overstate value, while excluding the acquired business could understate it. The filed purchase price is large relative to the $1.434 billion base equity value, so the net effect is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing filing and purchase-price schedule showing cash paid, acquired cash, new borrowings, transaction costs, earnout liability, assumed liabilities, and share effects; rebuild the bridge and OE forecast on a post-close perimeter.

audit_findings.title: The $52.2 million anchor must exclude investment and disposal gains that may also be represented in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.561 million unrealized gain plus $13.730 million disposal gain less $5.817 million impairment equals $36.474 million net pre-tax, 69.9% of the $52.2 million anchor; tax-adjusted effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained nonoperating gain inflates anchor OE and is then capitalized, while separately adding the related investment or proceeds in the bridge creates possible double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: The change in unrealized gain on investments in 2025 compared to 2024 was due to mark-to-market adjustments to adjust the value of the investments, including a $33.3 million increase in the value of the Company’s investment in Atlas.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed gains and impairment are demonstrated, but their inclusion in the $52.2 million OE anchor is unresolved because the exact reconciliation was not supplied. If the $36.474 million net pre-tax amount was retained, it is very large relative to the anchor and would materially overstate operating value. Removing the impairment works in the opposite direction, but the disclosed gains dominate before tax.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 net-income-to-OE reconciliation line by line, including tax effects, and rerun after consistently removing unrealized gains, impairments, disposal gains, equity-method results, and income associated with every separately added stake.

audit_findings.magnitude: June 30, 2026 NCI book balance $70.008 million, equal to 4.9% of base equity value or $1.48 per diluted share; six-month NCI earnings $3.258 million; full valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Common-attributable earnings are combined with consolidated depreciation, amortization, capital expenditures, working-capital flows, cash, and investments unless minority-owned amounts are allocated out.
audit_findings.evidence: The noncontrolling interest in our subsidiaries and their equity balances are reported separately in the consolidated financial statements, and activities of these subsidiaries are included therein.
audit_findings.explanation: NCI and its claim are demonstrated, but the record does not show how much of each OE adjustment or bridge asset belongs to minority holders. The $70.008 million book claim establishes relevant scale, but it is not a fair-value measure and cannot quantify the recurring OE mismatch. Materiality therefore remains uncertain rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile depreciation, amortization, capital expenditures, working-capital changes, cash, investments, and debt by subsidiary and ownership percentage; rerun using parent-attributable amounts or deduct a supported fair value for the minority claim.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not equal cash distributable to common shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: $253.2 million held by foreign subsidiaries, including $91.2 million exposed to potential withholding tax; the exposed pool equals 6.4% of base equity value or $1.93 per diluted share before applying any tax; actual leakage unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding taxes, ownership claims, legal restrictions, and required operating cash reduce the cash that can properly be added dollar-for-dollar in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our foreign subsidiaries held approximately $221.2 million of cash, cash equivalents, and investments, of which approximately $80.1 million would be subject to foreign withholding tax if distributed outside the country in which the related earnings were generated.
audit_findings.explanation: The foreign location and potential tax exposure are filed facts, but neither the applicable tax leakage nor the amount requiring repatriation is established. The $91.2 million is an exposed asset pool, not the tax itself. Because the bridge adds $439.975 million of cash and short-term investments without a location or operating-cash adjustment, a value overstatement is possible, but its materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30 cash and short-term-investment schedule by jurisdiction, legal owner, restriction, and operating requirement; calculate applicable withholding and other repatriation costs and rerun the bridge with only parent-available excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The failed liabilities parse could omit non-debt claims against added assets
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.372 million deferred-compensation investments, $23.844 million unrecognized tax benefits, and $45.724 million other long-term liabilities at June 30, 2026; overlap and bridge adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Investments included in stakes_net require matching deferred-compensation or other claimant liabilities to be netted; other debt-like claims may also reduce the equity bridge if not captured through OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We offset our obligations under the Deferred Compensation Plan primarily by investing in the actual underlying investments.
audit_findings.explanation: A failed parse does not itself demonstrate that a liability was omitted. The filing nevertheless confirms material claimant balances and that deferred-compensation investments economically offset plan obligations. The June obligation is not separately quantified, and the composition of the $260.5 million stakes_net is absent, so neither the existence nor materiality of a net bridge error can be established.
audit_findings.action: Map every component of stakes_net to the June 30 balance sheet and manually reconcile deferred-compensation obligations, tax contingencies, pension deficits, derivatives, and other long-term liabilities; net only those claims paired with added nonoperating assets and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-related amortization may represent recurring economic acquisition cost
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 acquisition-related amortization $22.227 million, equal to 42.6% of the $52.2 million anchor; six-month 2026 amortization $7.855 million; normalized economic cost unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back acquisition amortization while excluding recurring acquisition spending raises OE and operating PV without charging for the investment required to sustain acquisition-dependent growth.
audit_findings.evidence: A significant part of our growth strategy involves acquiring companies and businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: The amortization and acquisition-led strategy are demonstrated, but whether the entire accounting charge represents an ongoing economic cost is unresolved. Its scale relative to anchor OE, together with the completed ElevATE acquisition, makes the treatment reasonably capable of materially overstating value if acquisitions are necessary to maintain the forecast earnings base.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the precise amortization addback in the OE reconciliation, separate replacement acquisitions from expansion acquisitions, estimate normalized acquisition spending or an equivalent recurring charge from filed transactions, and rerun all scenarios with that charge retained.
